svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.20.9.4 Tying
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.20 MASONRY AND INSULATING CONCRETE FORM WALLS NOT IN CONTACT WITH THE GROUND
Tying

g.text: 17.8 mm² in section, 50 mm bent at each end, (3)
Ends within 25 mm of each face, in
Collar joint filled solid with mortar, (5)
Ties not more than 900 mm apart horizontally
Within 300 mm of openings, not more than
Ties within 100 mm below a floor or roof

Bottom of the floor or roof assembly, with

Cavity wall with wire ties, (7) to (9)

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Wythes tied with individual rod ties: the ties conform to
Sentences (3) to (6).
Other ties may be used where they give walls at least as
strong and durable.
Rod ties are corrosion-resistant, not less than 17.8 mm² in
cross-section, with not less than a 50 mm portion bent at
right angles at each end.
Rod ties extend to within 25 mm of the outer and inner faces,
are completely embedded in mortar except in a cavity, and are
staggered from course to course.
In walls other than cavity walls and veneer/backing walls, the
space between rod-tied wythes is completely filled with
mortar.
Those ties are within 300 mm of openings and not more than 900
mm apart around them, and elsewhere not more than 900 mm apart
horizontally and 460 mm vertically.
Cavity wall wire ties: not more than 900 mm apart horizontally
and 400 mm vertically, except as in Sentences (8) and (9).
Within 100 mm of the bottom of each floor or roof assembly,
where the cavity extends below it: not more than 600 mm apart
horizontally.
Within 300 mm of any opening: not more than 900 mm apart.
Drawn: tie ends red on the face, tie layouts one example within the limits. A: course above removed. 17.8 mm² is a 4.76 mm round rod.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.20.9.4. (page 9-145)
